# 好多鱼图文

Private self-media account matrix. Humans sign in with username/password. Authorized AI integrations use scoped Bearer credentials issued by the administrator.

Public documentation: /api-docs
OpenAPI: /openapi.json
API base: /api/v1

Only successfully published articles are recorded. Cumulative observations and daily period metrics are separate. Read the OpenAPI schema, use Idempotency-Key for writes, and verify saved records by ID. Never invent missing metrics. Do not request an administrator password for API access.

Atomic daily snapshot exception: GET /api/v1/snapshot?date=YYYY-MM-DD accepts exactly one explicit valid date; GET /api/v1/snapshot/index accepts no query parameters. Both are read-only current projections and never write business data or Notion. They require the existing matrix_session of the explicitly configured PUBLIC_BUSINESS_USER_ID, or anonymous public access only when PUBLIC_BUSINESS_MODE=1. PUBLIC_BUSINESS_USER_ID and DAILY_NOTES_OWNER_ID must be explicitly configured even in private mode. Owner sessions retain all-account visibility; anonymous scope follows existing configured accounts plus public-created accounts minus public-deleted accounts. Any Authorization header is rejected with 403, including Bearer/API keys; other logged-in users receive 403. No new API-key permission is provided.

Snapshot success is wrapped in data, with snapshot_format, projection=current, date, scope_id, timezone=Asia/Shanghai, generated_at, content_hash, and a nested data object containing todos, templates, notes, accounts, articles, observations, daily_metrics, habit30days. Notes use the existing public daily-note owner, exclude soft-deleted records, and contain no memo. Articles include run-date drafts, publication-day and observation/metric-linked records, preserving lifecycle, nulls and decoded pipeline JSON. habit30days covers D-29 through D, counts distinct completed days per current active template, and uses threshold 21. Empty dates still return current account/template frames and the habit window.

The index returns complete=true, scope_id, every real business date in ascending order with its daily content_hash, and index_hash. There is no recent-days cutoff or partial-success truncation. Hashes exclude generated_at, include scope, canonicalize object keys and entity collections, and preserve nested business-array order. This is not a historical database backup. Compare the union of current indexed dates and previously saved dates; reread changed and disappeared dates to detect old edits, final-record deletion and date moves. A changed scope_id requires rebaselining, never deletion inference. Each request is atomic including authorization, but index and daily reads can race: on a daily hash mismatch, reread the index and affected detail, and recheck the index before applying the batch.

Whole-request limits: 45 SQL calls including authorization/revision checks/retries, 4000 projected rows, 1MiB source projection JSON, 1000 indexed dates, 8MiB total hash input, 1MiB response, 100000 observed rows_read, and 50 accounts. Limits return 413 SNAPSHOT_LIMIT, never partial data; unavailable rows_read receipts return 503 SNAPSHOT_BUDGET. rows_read is observed after queries and is not a hard pre-query scan or CPU cap; edge CPU behavior remains unverified. Successful responses use Cache-Control: private, no-store and Vary: Cookie, Authorization.

Life/work notes: category defaults to life for legacy compatibility; category=work is independent. Snapshot v1 is unchanged; notes=all explicitly selects complete dual-category v2 and work-only dates. Backups are v8, retaining v1-v7 isolated empty-target restore compatibility.

Workbench additions: /note-entries supports multiple stable UUID life/work records per day (complete live list <=200/category/day), paged distinct dates, item reads, CAS PUT, explicit delete/restore, and editor-only metadata receipts. Stored server timestamps are preserved; legacy /daily-notes remains independent. /work-reminders?date returns items (<=100 live/day); PUT uses immutable date/source_key and <=16KiB summary; update the existing UUID for a repeated day/source. Both modules retain DAILY_NOTES_OWNER_ID session/public same-origin editing, save_id receipts and shared notes rate limits; Bearer provides no write capability. No new cron or external notification is configured.

GET /workbench-snapshot?date and /workbench-snapshot/index are a separate read-only format, haoduoyu-workbench-snapshot-v1. Existing snapshot v1/v2 stay unchanged. Both return a complete identical all-date entity/tombstone manifest plus undated memos, stable scope-qualified IDs, source timestamps, per-entity hashes, manifest_hash/global_content_hash; daily data contains todos, life_notes, work_notes, work_reminders, memo_groups, memos. Index date hashes match daily date_content_hash; daily content_hash also covers undated content. Deduplicate by scope_id/entity_id, preserve legacy/new identities, rebaseline changed scope, and recheck manifests before applying cross-request sync. Uses existing snapshot owner-session/public policy, rejects every Authorization header, additionally requires explicit MEMOS_OWNER_ID, reads every source completely, and shares the documented 45-SQL/4000-row/1MiB-source/1000-date/8MiB-hash/1MiB-response/100000-observed-rows_read/50-account bounds; 413/503 errors never mean partial success.

/account-profiles reads only authorized account mappings (<=1000, otherwise422). Optional profile_url on account creation/update is locally canonicalized for known Toutiao, Zhihu and WeChat public homepages; it never logs into or fetches platforms. Visible canonical duplicates return200/profile_reused:true; out-of-scope duplicates reveal no record. GET /backup now exports v9 with note_entries, work_reminders and account_profiles; v1-v8 restore remains operator-only, explicit and empty-target-only. No HTTP restore, platform tokens, Tencent integration or Notion automation change is introduced.

AI reports: OpenAPI describes GET /api/v1/ai-reports?offset=0, PUT /api/v1/ai-reports/{uuid}, and DELETE /api/v1/ai-reports/{uuid}. In PUBLIC_BUSINESS_MODE=1, anyone can read and write without identity authentication; author is self-reported, not verified. Public PUT requires Origin exactly equal to the site origin, X-Public-Business: 1, and application/json. Supply exactly author and content; conventionally start content with the work date YYYY-MM-DD on its first line (the server does not enforce the date). Generate a lowercase UUID once and retry the same normalized body with that UUID: 201 creates, 200 replays, and 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT signals different content. Lists return at most 100 items and has_more; increase offset by 100 to continue. Each item has content_hash, a lowercase SHA-256 digest of stable JSON over id, author, content and created_at. The user has approved deletion of any single report by any visitor in public mode. Deletion is permanent and cannot be recovered; author signatures are self-reported and unauthenticated. To delete, send DELETE with application/json {"expected_hash":"<content_hash from GET>","save_id":"<lowercase UUID for this operation>"}, same-origin Origin and X-Public-Business: 1. A stale expected_hash returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT; reread the list before deciding whether to retry. The same identity repeating the identical request with the same save_id replays success, unless a record with that ID exists again (409); using that save_id for a different request returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A missing report returns 404. After deletion, PUT with the same report UUID returns 409 AI_REPORT_DELETED to prevent resurrection by a delayed create retry. Author is 1–120 Unicode code points; content is at most 16 KiB UTF-8 after normalization and trimming; the JSON body is at most 256 KiB. Public writes, including rejected bodies and retries, are limited per owner and module per process to 60/minute and 2000/UTC day; this is not a global limit. Errors include 400 validation/JSON, 401/403 access, 404 invalid route/UUID, 413 body too large, 415 content type, 429 AI_REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT, 500 internal error, and 503 configuration unavailable. Error responses contain error.code, error.message and request_id. Explicit invalid credentials do not fall back to anonymous access. An owner session also works with Origin and CSRF on writes; Bearer keys do not grant access.
